scope: Measurement only. Unchanged readiness-gated burst and soak drivers/targets, same 0.109 image (sha256:bb15549ea9f32f1103c66879faa7599a89b8b3937f98a8980cf4e91b8cb73539, orgiq-middleware:cluster-0109-validation), DynamoDB Local/Redis/Postgres unchanged. Only the fixture BFF container budget varied (--cpus / --memory), matching middlewareCpu 1024/2048/4096 shapes. Local only, no cloud, no BFF/library code change. Launcher test-support/bff-cluster-containers.py and bff-cluster-capacity.mjs now read ORGIQ_BFF_CONTAINER_CPUS / ORGIQ_BFF_CONTAINER_MEMORY_MIB (default 1 / 1024, previous behaviour).
docker: Colima VM, 6 CPUs / 11.65 GiB; two BFFs capped at 4 CPUs each oversubscribe the VM with DynamoDB Local and the load driver.
caveat: Memory 4096 MiB (not 2048) was used for every run as requested. The 700 MiB server-memory-peak target is fixed; Node's heap limit scales with the container limit, so soak RSS (709-749 MiB) is not comparable to the 1 GiB runs (246 MiB). burst-2cpu was plain mode; others used metrics mode (store counters, ORGIQ_BFF_CONTAINER_STORE_METRICS=1), which adds overhead; burst-2cpu-metrics is the same-mode 2 CPU comparison.
note: Arrays are [p50 or a, p95 or b] as named in the table in capacity-progress.md; see *-driver.log and *-result.json for raw values.
finding: BFF CPU peaked 98-128% of a 200-400% cap: CPU was not saturated at 2 or 4 CPUs. The AWS SDK DynamoDB HTTP agent is capped at 50 sockets (dynamoHttp.socketLimit) with ~1,200-1,400 requests queued at peak on every run, regardless of CPU. chat-members Query p95 buckets sit at 512-1024 ms. That socket queue, not BFF CPU, now bounds chat p95.
verdict: No size passed all targets. 2 CPU: burst fails invite/accept/chat/health, soak fails chat p95 and memory target (heap artifact). 4 CPU: burst fails chat p95 (1,465 ms) and both health p99; soak fails chat p95 (802 ms) and memory target. Not acceptance.
